column3: The Hebrew uses singular collective names for the Reubenite and Gadite; BSB uses plural “Reubenites” and “Gadites.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “these many days” and names the charge of the LORD’s commandment; BSB has “All this time” and “the charge given you.”
The Hebrew repeats “and now,” commands them to turn and go, and calls their dwellings “tents”; BSB has one “now,” says they “may return,” and uses “homes.”
The Hebrew says Moses “commanded” the commandment and law; BSB says he “gave” them.
The Hebrew says “their tents”; BSB says “their homes.”
The Hebrew does not explicitly repeat an object for Moses’ and Joshua’s giving and calls the dwellings “tents”; BSB supplies “land” twice and says “homes.”
The Hebrew has both “said” and “saying” and names “your tents”; BSB has one “saying” and “your homes.”
The Hebrew uses “according to the mouth of the LORD” and “by the hand of Moses”; BSB says “according to the command of the LORD through Moses.”
The Hebrew repeats “altar” and calls it “great in appearance”; BSB uses “altar” once and calls it “imposing.”
The Hebrew says the altar is “opposite” the land of Canaan; BSB says “on the border of” that land.
The Hebrew explicitly names “the sons of Israel” twice; BSB begins with “they” and then says “the whole congregation of Israel.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats “one chief” distributively and calls the divisions “thousands”; BSB has “one family leader” and “clans.”
The Hebrew has both “spoke” and “saying”; BSB gives a single “said.”

The Hebrew repeats the breach-of-faith root in noun and verb and twice places “today” with turning back and rebelling; BSB uses “breach of faith ... committed” and places its first “today” with that breach.
The Hebrew states that a plague was in the congregation; BSB explicitly makes the sin the cause with “It even brought a plague.”
The Hebrew says “today” with both turning back and rebelling; BSB first uses “now” and then “today.”
The Hebrew repeats the verb for rebelling in both prohibitions; BSB states it once for the LORD and “us.”
The Hebrew repeats the unfaithfulness root and refers to Achan as “he, one man”; BSB says “was ... unfaithful” and explicitly repeats Achan’s name.
The Hebrew separately says they answered and spoke and calls the divisions “thousands”; BSB uses one “answered” and “clans.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly names the LORD in the turning-away clause and uses singular “burnt offering” and “grain offering”; BSB has “Him” and plural “offerings.”
The Hebrew says “tomorrow,” repeats “saying,” and explicitly names “our sons”; BSB has “in the future,” one “say,” and “ours.”
The Hebrew explicitly names “our sons”; BSB uses “ours.”
The Hebrew uses singular “a burnt offering” and “a sacrifice”; BSB has plural “burnt offerings” and “sacrifices.”
The Hebrew repeats the service root in a verb and noun, says “tomorrow,” and explicitly names “our sons”; BSB has “worship,” “in the future,” and “ours.”
The Hebrew says “our generations” and uses singular “a burnt offering” and “a sacrifice”; BSB says “our descendants” and uses plural offering terms.
The Hebrew explicitly names the LORD three times; BSB uses “Him” for the middle occurrence. The Hebrew has singular offering terms where BSB has plural ones.
The Hebrew says the words were “good in their eyes”; BSB expresses this as being satisfied.
